commit_message: [Merged] Added the incremental loading system for the CID driver. Tested using my own unit test code.
pr_title: [cid] Add boundary check for fd_select in incremental interface
pr_description:
When loading glyphs via the FreeType incremental interface, the `fd_select` value read from the callback-supplied glyph data must be validated before being used as an index into the font dictionary array.

This change adds the required bounds check in `cid_load_glyph()` for the incremental code path (`FT_CONFIG_OPTION_INCREMENTAL`). If `fd_select` is greater than or equal to `cid->num_dicts`, the function now logs an appropriate trace message and returns `FT_Err_Invalid_Offset`.

A special case is handled for `fd_select == 0xFF` (fd_bytes==1) or `fd_select == 0xFFFF` (fd_bytes==2), which is a common convention indicating that a CID has no charstring to render — analogous to GID 0xFFFF in TrueType fonts. This case is reported at TRACE1 level rather than TRACE0 to distinguish it from a genuine out-of-range error.

Fixes issue #1394.

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

intro_commit_message: Added the incremental loading system for the CID driver. Tested using my own unit test code.
fix_commit_message:
[cid] Add boundary check in incremental interface.

* src/cid/cidgload.c (cid_load_glyph) [FT_CONFIG_OPTION_INCREMENTAL]:
  Validate `fd_select`.

Fixes issue #1394.
agent_reasoning: Without this check, an attacker who controls the incremental interface callback can supply an `fd_select` value that is >= `cid->num_dicts`. This value is then used as an array index into `face->subrs` without any bounds validation, causing an out-of-bounds heap read. The fix validates `fd_select` immediately after it is extracted from the callback data and before it is used as an array index, returning `FT_Err_Invalid_Offset` for any out-of-range value.
